author: c2-sql-edu-critic (independent education critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; reviewed commit 8a7daa17)

findings.claim: E1: The ambiguous-column translation always suggests the alias s ("…for example s.instructor_id"), whatever aliases the learner used. In Activity 3 the task step says "Sort by instructor_id, then course_id", and hint 2 says "give the instructor's id first", so a learner who follows them writes ORDER BY instructor_id and hits the ambiguous ERROR. The feedback then suggests s.instructor_id, but s is not an alias in this query. Following it gives a second ERROR ("s. names a table or alias that FROM and JOIN do not define"). Run back to back in one session (the task-literal ORDER BY, then the suggested s.instructor_id), so the fix the feedback names is wrong for this query on the activity's main path.
findings.recommendation: In page-build/controller.js (SQLCHK.explain), build the example from an alias the learner's FROM or JOIN actually defines, or say "put the alias you gave that table, such as the i in instructors AS i, in front of it". In the task step, write "the instructor's instructor_id" so qualifying is part of the instruction.

findings.claim: §4 (at most 120 words per teach step) and cognitive load. No gate counts teaching words (T08 and the QA harness have no such check), so this count is the critic's own: the prose of [data-pep-teaching], leaving out pre blocks and figures. By that count Activity 2's teaching prose runs to about 164 words, not counting the example, its result table and the two data tables. It packs the inner join, ON, a review link, aliases, qualifying, the ambiguous ERROR, duplicate matches, dropped rows and a JDBC aside into one step for a learner meeting joins for the first time.
findings.recommendation: Cut to 120 words or fewer. The alias and qualifying paragraph could move to Activity 1, which already introduces table-dot-column, and the JDBC sentence could move to the On the job card.

findings.claim: F5/B5: One editor has three names and two verdicts. Output opens with "(lesson simulator, not real PostgreSQL server)", the bar says "Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables", the status line says "SQL practice editor", and after a run that stops with a PostgreSQL ERROR the Problems tab still says "No problems found by the lesson checker". This is what remains of the new-learner review's F5 finding on this page: the feedback now says "PostgreSQL cannot tell which one you mean" right under an Output header that says "not real PostgreSQL server".
findings.recommendation: Use one name everywhere, such as "practice editor". The "not real" tail of the Output header comes from EDITOR.language = 'PostgreSQL server' in page-build/controller.js, and its "lesson simulator" prefix and the Problems sentence come from the shared shell. Change the page-owned part now; ask for a shell version that, after an ERROR, says "No problems before Run; see Output for the ERROR" and drops "not real".

findings.claim: Semantic leakage through the task and hints: Activity 3's step 2 gives the SELECT list as code ("i.name AS instructor and c.title AS course"). Step 1 fixes the table order. Hint 1 repeats the table order, and hint 2 dictates the ON pairing and the sort keys. With the worked example in the same shape, the only thing left for the learner is typing.
findings.recommendation: State the output columns by meaning ("a column instructor with the instructor's name and a column course with the course title") and let the learner choose aliases. Keep hint 2 to a reasoning step about which column links the two tables.

findings.claim: E1/F5: The Problems panel files ordinary SQL mistakes under the label "Not in this practice editor": a typo ("SELEC * FROM students;"), a missing comma between two VALUES rows and a missing semicolon all show that label, and so does the untouched starter ("Write at least one SQL statement, ending with a semicolon"), before the first Run. Reproduced on all eight pages of the module: a missing semicolon at the end of line 3 (SELECT name / FROM students / WHERE city = 'Leeds' / SELECT 2;) shows "Ln 4 Not in this practice editor ... could not read the statement near select". The editor's own limits list says the label means "a limit of this page, not a sign that your SQL is wrong", so a beginner whose SQL is wrong is told it may be fine.
findings.recommendation: In page-build/controller.js, where EDITOR.kindLabels maps the adapter's limit kind to "Not in this practice editor", show parse problems under their own learner label, such as "Check your SQL", and keep "Not in this practice editor" for genuine subset limits (WITH, COPY, CREATE TABLE). If the adapter cannot tell the two apart, reword the matching LIMITS sentence in page-build/build.mjs so it no longer says the label is never a sign of wrong SQL.

findings.claim: E5 (practice-feedback-policy 1.3): Parse problems point at the line after the mistake, not at the line to change. A missing comma at the end of line 2 of a multi-row INSERT is reported as "Ln 3 ... near "("", and a missing semicolon at the end of line 4 is reported as "Ln 5 ... near "select"", which is the policy's own counter-example. Reproduced on all eight pages: a missing semicolon at the end of line 3 is reported at Ln 4. The message does not say that the place to look is the end of the line before.
findings.recommendation: Where the adapter reports "could not read the statement near" on the first token of a line, have the page controller (page-build/controller.js) add "Check the end of the line before it too, for a missing comma or semicolon", or point the Ln marker at the previous non-blank line. The adapter is copied unchanged, so the wording fix belongs in this module's controller unless a new adapter version changes the location.

findings.claim: E3 / check wording: when only the secondary sort is missing, the second check, "The result shows exactly name and course_id, sorted by name, then course_id", stays unticked even though the columns are exactly right. Its id is "join", but it checks no join. Both checks mention order. The near-miss feedback itself is now good ("Almost. … add course_id after name"), which resolves the review's main complaint.
findings.recommendation: Split the checks by what they verify: one for the 9 rows and columns, one for "sorted by name, then course_id", and tick each on its own.

findings.claim: B1/D3: Hint 2 ("ORDER BY takes two keys separated by a comma") and the Activity 3 feedback ("add the course's id as a second key") use "key" for a sort column, on a page whose joins are built on primary and foreign keys.
findings.recommendation: Say "two sort columns" instead of "two keys".

findings.claim: B2: The retry option "enrollments LEFT JOIN students WHERE students.student_id IS NULL" is the anti-join pattern taught in the next topic. It is a distractor, but its explanation ("looks for enrollments whose student is missing") needs that later idea.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a distractor built from this page's ideas, for example "enrollments INNER JOIN courses".

findings.claim: B5: Shared controller and build wording. (1) Confidence choices read Low / Medium / High; DESIGN.md "Assessment: options, confidence, feedback" sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". (2) A wrong prediction opens "Your guess was not this time; the right answer is marked.", which drops a word. (3) The end-of-page message reads "Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are not done yet".
findings.recommendation: In page-build/build.mjs (CONF) use Guessing / Fairly sure / Certain. In page-build/controller.js write "Your guess was not right this time; the right answer is marked." and join several open activities as "Activities 2, 3 and 4 are not done yet".

findings.claim: G7/F1: On a headless Chromium 570 x 1000 viewport, opening the page from file:// leaves it scrolled 157 px down with the hash #activity-1. The topic title, progress line and Topic objectives are above the first screen, which starts at the lesson-path row. At 1280 px the scroll was 0 on seven pages and 121 px on inner-and-left-joins. This was measured only under file:// in headless Chromium, and the cause was not found: history.replaceState did not throw when called after load, and turning off scroll anchoring did not change the result.
findings.recommendation: Check this in a desktop browser and in the platform embed. If it reproduces, do not set location.hash on first load (restore scroll to 0, or skip the hash when there is none), so the first screen shows the title and Topic objectives.
